insight: npm run build rewrites next-env.d.ts imports from .next/dev/types to .next/types (and next dev flips it back). The file is committed, so a verification build dirties the tree. Revert it with git checkout -- next-env.d.ts before pushing rather than committing the churn.

NSP had no VERSION file, so gstack-version-bump classify returns DRIFT_UNEXPECTED (a false positive: it compares package.json 0.1.0 against an absent VERSION treated as 0.0.0.0). Not a manual-edit bypass. As of v0.1.0.1 VERSION and CHANGELOG.md exist, so classify should return FRESH from here on.

playwright.config.ts starts its own dev server on port 3017 with reuseExistingServer:false, so npx playwright test needs no manual server and will not collide with npm run dev on 3000. Full suite runs in about 5 seconds.

In next dev, Next.js injects a dev-tools indicator as the first unclassed div in body. In a full-page browse screenshot it renders mid-page (fixed positioning against the stitched image) and can overlap real content, looking like a CSS bug. Verify with $B html on the element before chasing it; it is absent from next build.

browse click reports the URL BEFORE the navigation it triggered (Clicked X -> now at <previous page>). On a multi-step flow this reads as if a click did not land. Confirm position with a separate $B url call rather than trusting the click line.

For disabled buttons in the NSP paper/ink palette, use ink text on --color-line (#c8c8c8) at ~11:1, not white on --color-muted (#8a8a8a) at ~3.45:1. The grey fill still reads as inactive while the label stays legible in daylight. Pair it with an aria-describedby hint naming the unblock condition instead of enabling the control.

A position:sticky bottom-0 bar renders at its viewport-pinned spot in a full-page browse screenshot, so it looks like it overlaps mid-page content even when it does not. Do not judge overlap from the stitched image: scroll to bottom and compare getBoundingClientRect().bottom of the last control against the bar rect top. Negative difference means clear.

Verify label/input association with label.control===input and button hints with getAttribute(aria-describedby) resolving to real text, rather than trusting the JSX. Force error branches by stubbing window.fetch in the page before clicking, which proved role=alert actually renders on the NSP submit error.

Enabling viewport-fit=cover to make one env(safe-area-inset-*) term non-zero obligates the layout to pad top, bottom, AND side insets on every route. Applying side insets inside a max-w capped mx-auto shell is actively wrong: it subtracts from content width instead of moving the shell off the edge. For a centered fixed-width column with no edge-to-edge art, leave viewport-fit at its default and clear sticky bars with a spacer.

When a control is gated on exact equality with fixture data, any hint text saying to match a value shown above must be checked against what actually renders. NSP recovery told users to match the mock PFMS spelling that the component never displayed, making the flow completable only by reading source. Write the test to read the target value off the page rather than hardcoding it, so removing the value fails the test instead of passing on fixture knowledge.

tsconfig.tsbuildinfo is generated by next build/dev in NSP and was not in .gitignore, so it shows as untracked after any build and can dirty a ship verification gate. Added to .gitignore in v0.1.1.0. next-env.d.ts still flips between .next/dev/types and .next/types imports on build vs dev and needs git checkout before pushing.
